# nonNaN

<link-summary>Checks whether a value is **not** the `NaN` number.</link-summary>

<web-summary>nonNaN() — Checks whether a value is **not** the `NaN` number. apps-script-utils, English.</web-summary>

<tldr>
<p>Module: <code>lang/number</code> · Since: 1.11.0</p>
</tldr>

```typescript
function nonNaN<T>(value: T | number): value is T;
```

`nonNaN(value)` is the same test as `!isNaN(value)`, written so that a guard clause reads as a sentence rather than as a negation.

Nothing is coerced first, which is where this differs from the global `isNaN`: that one converts its argument, so `isNaN("abc")` and `isNaN(undefined)` both report `true`.

`isX` and `nonX` answer a question and never interrupt control flow; `requireX` and `requireNonX` hand the value back or throw. The scheme is explained in [](validation-conventions.md).

## Parameters

| Parameter | Type          | Description         |
| :-------- | :------------ | :------------------ |
| `value`   | `T \| number` | The value to check. |

## Returns

`boolean` — `true` when the value is not the `NaN` number; otherwise `false`.

In TypeScript the guard narrows `value` to `T` inside the branch.

## Examples

### What passes and what does not

```javascript
nonNaN(0); // => true
nonNaN("abc"); // => true
nonNaN(undefined); // => true
nonNaN(NaN); // => false
nonNaN(0 / 0); // => false
```
